did_you_know.text: In the traditional Hebrew calendar, the third month is Sivan. That is why Shavuot, which commemorates the giving of the Torah, falls in Sivan.
The Hebrew word nesher may refer to an eagle or another large bird of prey, not necessarily the modern eagle. The image emphasizes protection, carrying, and bringing someone to safety.
The word segullah here means a treasured possession or special property. This is one of the ancient sources of the word’s modern Hebrew meaning.
In the Bible, the word holy often means set apart for a particular purpose, not only morally pure. Thus, “a holy nation” describes a people with a special mission.
The word yovel in this verse is connected with a ram’s horn and its blast. Only after the signal sounded could the people go up the mountain.

The phrase kolot uvrakim is usually translated as “thunder and lightning,” but kolot literally means sounds or loud voices. The description combines sound, light, and cloud to create a powerful and frightening scene.
The phrase “growing louder and louder” describes a sound that increases in strength. It creates the feeling that the moment is gradually reaching its climax.
The warning not to break through toward the mountain teaches that even curiosity needs limits. Clear boundaries can protect people in a dangerous or sacred place.
